item.title: #1 [0/100] Longitudinal viral load trajectories predict cervical lesion risk in women with persistent human papillomavirus infection: A prospective cohort study.

Authors: Zhou Y, Chen S, Zhang Y, Jiang Y, Xiao M, Xin X, Shi Z, Zhang L
Journal: Cancer | DOI: 10.1002/cncr.70648
Published: 2026-Dec-01
PMID: 43069728



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is central to cervical lesion development, but single viral-load measurements may not capture heterogeneous viral dynamics. This study characterized longitudinal viral-load trajectories among women with persistent infection and evaluated their associations with cervical lesions and incremental predictive value beyond baseline factors. METHODS: In this prospective cohort of 1502 HPV-positive women followed at approximately 6-month intervals, latent class growth analysis using actual follow-up time was conducted among 624 women with type-specific persistent infection. Associations between trajectory group and any cervical lesion (low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion or high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion [HSIL]) were assessed using multivariable logistic regression; HSIL was explored using Firth-penalized regression. Discrimination, calibration, and decision-curve analysis were used to assess incremental predictive performance. RESULTS: Of 1170 women with classifiable outcomes, 624 had persistent infection. Four trajectories were identified: low stable (39.6%), moderate declining (18.9%), moderate increasing (29.8%), and persistently high (11.7%). Any-lesion prevalence was 10.9%, 17.8%, 74.2%, and 90.4%, respectively (p < .001). Compared with the low-stable group, fully adjusted odds ratios (ORs) were 1.95 (95% CI, 1.02-3.74), 29.66 (95% CI, 16.75-52.51), and 124.29 (95% CI, 47.30-326.60) for the other groups, respectively. The persistently high group was also associated with HSIL (OR, 9.47; 95% CI, 3.18-33.09). The optimism-corrected area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) increased from 0.713 for the base model to 0.888 for both the simple longitudinal and trajectory models and 0.899 for the joint model. CONCLUSIONS: Longitudinal HPV viral-load dynamics identified clinically distinct risk phenotypes. Moderate-increasing and persistently high trajectories were strongly associated with cervical lesions, whereas longitudinal information improved discrimination beyond baseline measurements. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

Authors: Saniasiaya J, van der Meer G
Journal: The Annals of otology, rhinology, and laryngology | DOI: 10.1177/00034894261508792
Published: 2026-Nov-26
PMID: 43094457



Abstract:
UNLABELLED: Deep interarytenoid notch (DIN), a subclassification of type 1 laryngeal cleft (LC) has been found to cause dysphagia and aspiration in children, necessitating long-term feeding assistance. Various surgical interventions have shown promising results, although the outcomes and complications remain unknown. OBJECTIVE: We aim to investigate the outcome of surgical interventions for DIN in children. DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Google Scholar, and Scopus databases were searched from inception to May 31, 2025. RESULTS: Five studies were identified, involving a total of 117 children with a mean age of 22.4 months. DIN was diagnosed following an airway and swallowing assessment. All included children were trialled with feeding therapy before surgical interventions. Interarytenoid injection laryngoplasty (IL) was the favoured technique in 98.3% of included children. A statistically significant improvement in post-surgical interventions was observed across the included studies. 7.7% reported persistent symptoms requiring endoscopic surgical repair. No major or minor complications were reported. CONCLUSION: Surgical interventions, notably interarytenoid IL, demonstrated significant improvement and resolution of symptoms; early surgical interventions in children with DIN may improve dysphagia, alleviating the need for assisted feeding. Yet, multicentre, large, prospective, controlled trials comparing various treatment modalities are imperative to determine the efficacy of interventions for DIN in children.

Authors: Danis DO, Dalal K, Siegel R, Buffington K, Bharathi R, O'Leary M, Scott AR
Journal: The Annals of otology, rhinology, and laryngology | DOI: 10.1177/00034894261509205
Published: 2026-Nov-26
PMID: 43094453



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study presents a case series of patients who presented to the emergency department with pharyngeal foreign bodies and describes the success rate of awake removal in a clinic setting using topical anesthetic and flexible fiberoptic laryngoscopy (FFL). METHODS: Case series with retrospective chart review. The billing database of an urban, academic, tertiary otolaryngology clinic was queried to identify patients presenting for evaluation of odynophagia from suspect upper aerodigestive foreign body. All patients with visualized foreign body were managed with an identical technique for bedside removal. RESULTS: From 2020 to 2026, 36 cases (25 female, 11 male) were evaluated for pharyngeal foreign body and underwent bedside removal attempts using a 2-person approach, where 1 operator performs FFL, while another manually retracts the tongue, and uses curved Kelly Forceps to remove the foreign body. Foreign bodies consisted of a fishbone (0.2-3 cm) in 35 cases and a metal bristle in 1 case. The most common foreign body location was in the tongue base/vallecula in 26 cases (72%). Common presenting symptoms were odynophagia, throat discomfort, and foreign body sensation. 29/30 (97%) of adult cases had successful bedside removal. In 1 failed attempt, the patient swallowed the foreign body prior to removal. Only 2 pediatric cases (4 and 7 years) had successful bedside removal, whereas 3 pediatric cases (19 months-8 years) failed awake attempts at removal. CONCLUSION: Pharyngeal foreign bodies require timely removal given risk for serious complications. We found that the curvature of Kelly forceps is suitable in awake and upright patients. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: IV.

Authors: Maffezzoli M, Monaca F, Cantale O, Gomez-Randulfe I, Teoh A, Htun L, Gregory M, Holden C, Oludipe M, Mawella R, et al.
Journal: The oncologist | DOI: 10.1093/oncolo/oyag469
Published: 2026-Nov-25
PMID: 43094069



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Thyroid transcription factor-1 (TTF-1) is routinely assessed in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) as a diagnostic marker. Evidence suggests that TTF-1 may also have prognostic relevance in metastatic NSCLC (aNSCLC). We investigated the prognostic impact of TTF-1 expression in aNSCLC receiving first-line immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based therapy and its interplay with PD-L1. METHODS: This was a multicentre retrospective real-world study including patients with aNSCLC treated at five UK institutions with first-line ICI monotherapy or chemoimmunotherapy (CT+ICI) between 2017 and 2025. Outcomes were analysed according to TTF-1 status and PD-L1 expression, primarily in patients with adenocarcinoma (ADK). Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) was included as an exploratory comparator. RESULTS: Among 823 patients, 288 (35.0%) were TTF-1 negative (TTF1-) and 535 (65.0%) TTF-1 positive (TTF1+). TTF1- tumours included ADK (121, 42.0%) and SCC (167, 58.0%). TTF1-/ADK had shorter PFS (5.79 vs 9.90 months, HR 1.55, 95% CI 1.25-1.93, p < 0.001) and OS (11.12 vs 19.08 months, HR 1.58, 95% CI 1.26-1.98, p < 0.001) than TTF1+/ADK. Exploratory comparisons showed that TTF1-/SCC had poorer outcomes than TTF1+/ADK, although not different compared to TTF1-/ADK. In multivariable analyses focused on ADK, TTF-1 positivity remained independently associated with improved PFS (p=0.001) and OS (p<0.001). The prognostic association of TTF-1 was most pronounced in the PD-L1 1-49% subgroup and interaction testing confirmed significant heterogeneity between PD-L1 < 1% and 1-49%. CONCLUSIONS: TTF1-/ADK showed worse outcomes, with the strongest prognostic association in the PD-L1 1-49% subgroup. These findings support further investigation of prognostic heterogeneity and require independent validation.

Authors: Xu L, Ai X, Liu S, Quan T, Shen J, Yang Y, Chen Z, Mao YP, Sun Y, Zhou G, et al.
Journal: The oncologist | DOI: 10.1093/oncolo/oyag461
Published: 2026-Nov-25
PMID: 43094055



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nuclear protein in testis carcinoma (NUTC) is a rare and aggressive malignancy driven by NUTM1 rearrangement. While previous studies have focused on Western populations, data on Chinese NUTC remain scarce. METHODS: We screened 1,012 medical records from a single cancer center's intelligence platform. Chinese patients with pathologically confirmed NUTC were included. The clinicopathological characteristics of Chinese NUTC were compared with that of Western population. Cox regression model was performed to identify variables associated with survival outcomes. RESULTS: Between 2017-2023, 68 Chinese patients who met the eligible criteria were enrolled. The median age was 40.5 years (range, 1-79), which is older than the reported from Western patients in the NUT Midline Carcinoma Registry. 41 (60.3%) Chinese patients had head and neck origin compared to the thoracic-dominant origin in Western NUTC (P =0.02). After a median follow-up of 36.3 months, median progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) times of the whole cohort were 7.1 (95%CI: 5.1-9.1) and 11.8 (95%CI: 9.2-14.5) months, respectively. Further analysis revealed that patients with tumors of head and neck region had significantly better survival than that of thoracic region (Hazard ratio =1.81, P =0.04). Other prognostic factors included tumor size, lymph node and/or organ metastasis at diagnosis, expression level of Ki-67. For treatment-related factors, in addition to the reception of surgery, administration of radiotherapy was also an essential prognostic factor (Hazard ratio =0.22, P <0.01) . CONCLUSION: This study outlines distinct clinicopathological features of Chinese NUTC, and highlights radiotherapy as an effective treatment for NUTC.

Authors: Finnegan E, Olson BG, Moore EJ
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70551
Published: 2026-Nov-25
PMID: 43085959



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The incidence of oropharyngeal carcinoma (OPSCC) has increased in recent decades. T4 staging in OPSCC remains a poor prognostic factor, with the optimal treatment for T4 OPSCC unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare primary operative and nonoperative treatment in patients with T4 OPSCC. METHODS: Searches were conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Cochrane Library through September 2024. Studies comparing primary operative with nonoperative management for T4 OPSCC were included. Random effect models generated pooled risk ratios and hazard ratios. RESULTS: Five non-randomized cohort studies involving 10 158 patients were included, largely comprised of patients with resectable T4a disease. Of these, 23% (n = 2333) received operative management, and 77% (n = 7405) received nonoperative management. Operative management was associated with improved overall survival (OS) (HR 0.57; 95% CI 0.41-0.80; p = 0.001), disease-specific survival (DSS) (HR 0.44; 95% CI 0.31-0.74; p = 0.001), and disease-free survival (DFS) (HR 0.48; 95% CI 0.26-0.72; p = 0.001). No significant differences in overall recurrence rates were found. Subgroup analysis showed reduced recurrence for p16-positive patients receiving surgery. Functional outcomes and complications were similar between surgical and nonoperative management groups. CONCLUSION: This study supports a potential association between operative management and improved OS, DSS, and DFS in patients with T4 OPSCC. Among patients with p16-positive tumors, operative treatment appeared to be associated with lower observed recurrence rates, while no difference in recurrence was observed in the overall cohort. Further high-quality evidence is needed to confirm these findings and inform treatment planning.

Authors: Anderson NC, Berth SH
Journal: BMJ (Clinical research ed.) | DOI: 10.1136/bmj-2026-085090
Published: 2026-Nov-25
PMID: 43085813



Abstract:
Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction characterised by fluctuating fatigable weakness of skeletal muscles. Advances have led to the identification of distinct antibody subtypes and expanding therapeutic options, transforming myasthenia gravis from a disease of significant morbidity and mortality to one that is increasingly manageable. This review presents a comprehensive overview of myasthenia gravis, including its epidemiology, pathogenesis, classification, diagnostic strategies, and treatment modalities. Established therapies are discussed, including acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, corticosteroids, conventional oral immunosuppressants, intravenous immunoglobulin, plasma exchange, B cell depleting agents, complement inhibitors, neonatal fragment crystallisable receptor inhibitors, and thymectomy. A dedicated section highlights emerging treatments. Special considerations for pregnancy, myasthenic crisis, and individualised treatment approaches are emphasised. Physician-patient communication is highlighted as a critical factor in optimising adherence and outcomes. Effective integration of novel therapies into clinical practice depends on a clear understanding of their mechanisms, safety profiles, and applicability across diverse patient populations. As therapeutic complexity increases, improved clinical outcomes will require continued refinement of clinical tools, treatment algorithms, optimal communication strategies, and robust data to guide evidence based decision making.

Authors: Lu ZJ, Yang Q, Yang ZC, Chen QY, Liu LT, Sun R, Mo HY, Luo DH, Liu SL, Guo SS, et al.
Journal: ESMO open | DOI: 10.1016/j.esmoop.2026.108610
Published: 2026-Nov-25
PMID: 43085179



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with stage IV locoregionally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma (LA-NPC) remain at high risk of recurrence and distant metastasis despite intensity-modulated radiotherapy and concurrent cisplatin-based chemotherapy. Paclitaxel plus platinum (TP) has yielded encouraging activity. This randomized, open-label phase II trial evaluated whether concurrent TP could improve progression-free survival (PFS) compared with standard high-dose cisplatin (DDP) during chemoradiotherapy. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Patients with stage IV LA-NPC were randomly assigned 1 : 1 to concurrent TP (paclitaxel plus cisplatin every 4 weeks for two cycles; planned cumulative concurrent cisplatin dose, 160 mg/m2) or DDP (cisplatin every 3 weeks for three cycles; planned cumulative concurrent cisplatin dose, 300 mg/m2) during chemoradiotherapy. The primary endpoint was 3-year PFS in the intention-to-treat population. RESULTS: Between February 2017 and September 2019, 184 patients were enrolled (92 patients per group). Median follow-up was 47.6 months. The 3-year PFS rates were 68.2% [95% confidence interval (CI) 58.6-77.8] with TP and 72.8% (95% CI 63.8-81.8) with DDP [stratified hazard ratio (HR) 1.16, 95% CI 0.71-1.90, Plog-rank = 0.56]. The stratified HR for overall survival (OS) was 0.38 (95% CI 0.13-1.09, P = 0.07). Given the limited number of deaths, no OS advantage of TP can be concluded. The cumulative incidence of locoregional relapse and distant metastasis did not differ between groups. The DDP group had higher rates of any-grade nausea, vomiting, anorexia, constipation, and thrombocytopenia (all P < 0.05), whereas grade 3-4 neutropenia was numerically higher with TP (22.0% versus 13.5%, P = 0.14). Late toxicities did not differ significantly (all P ≥ 0.12). CONCLUSIONS: With a lower planned cumulative concurrent cisplatin dose in the TP arm, TP did not demonstrate an improvement in PFS compared with standard DDP in concurrent chemoradiotherapy for stage IV LA-NPC. These findings do not support replacing standard DDP with this reduced-cisplatin TP schedule and do not exclude a potential benefit of adding paclitaxel to an equivalent-dose cisplatin backbone.

item.title: #9 [0/100] Prenatal developmental toxicity of the 70% ethanolic extract of defatted Lepidium sativum L. seeds in Wistar rats.

Authors: Aragie TG, Asres K, Ergete W, Woldekidan S, Abebe A, Sisay B, Seyoum G
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0363832
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43084588



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Lepidium sativum Linn. seeds are widely consumed for medicinal and nutritional purposes, including among pregnant women; however, its safety profile during gestation remains inadequately defined. Therefore, this study evaluated the prenatal developmental toxicity of Lepidium sativum seeds in rats. METHODS: A total of five groups of pregnant Wistar rats were employed to evaluate the prenatal developmental effects of Lepidium sativum seed extract in two independent experimental arms. Treatments were administered via oral gavage during critical period of organogenesis (gestational day 12 [GD12] with the aim to evaluate the extract's effect on embryonic development. In GD12 experiment, each group containing a specific number of rats: group I and V consisted of ten rats each, while groups II, III, and IV included nine rats per group. Separate cohorts were examined on GD20 to capture near term developmental outcomes and late-stage developmental effects of the extract. The number of pregnant rats available for GD20 subgroup was ten in groups I, IV, and V, nine in group II, and seven in group III respectively. In both studies, groups I- III served as experimental groups and were given 250 mg/kg, 500 mg/kg, and 1000 mg/kg of the extract respectively during GD6-12. While, groups IV and V were pair-fed and ad libitum controls respectively. One-way ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc test was used to compare the groups, and statistical significance was declared at p < 0.05. RESULTS: In the GD12 subgroup, embryos from 1000 mg/kg of the extract exhibited significantly lower morphological scores in the embryonic heart (p < 0.01), otic (p = 0.002), and olfactory (p = 0.004) systems. A higher incidence of stillbirths and low birthweight pups was observed in 1000 mg/kg treated rats of GD20. Additionally, brain ventricular dilation was observed in 8% of fetuses from groups treated with 1000 mg/kg compared to the controls (p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Oral administration of Lepidium sativum seed extract during gestational day 6-12 at 500 mg/kg and 1000 mg/kg doses was associated with significant developmental delays in rat embryos. The extract also resulted in a higher number of stillbirths, low birthweight, and developmental delays in rat fetuses.

Authors: Simo N, Paredes A, Villanueva Á, Ghilotti J, Llena C
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0363657
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43084564



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This in vitro study evaluated the effect of irrigation protocols based on 5.25% sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) or 200 ppm hypochlorous acid (HOCl), used alone or combined with 17% ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA), on smear layer removal, open dentinal tubules and erosion of root canal dentin. METHODS: Forty-five palatal or distal roots of human molars were instrumented to size 50/.06 and randomly allocated to NaOCl + EDTA, NaOCl, HOCl + EDTA or HOCl (n = 10 each) or to a saline negative control (n = 5). Canals received 2 mL of irrigant after each instrument and a final sequence with 3 mL of each solution for 20 s. Root thirds were examined by scanning electron microscopy. A trained, calibrated and blinded examiner (weighted κ = 0.88) scored smear layer and erosion on ordinal scales; open tubules were quantified by digital image segmentation. RESULTS: Smear layer scores differed among groups only in the middle third (p = 0.013), where NaOCl + EDTA left less smear layer than NaOCl alone (p = 0.008); HOCl + EDTA did not differ significantly from HOCl alone or from NaOCl + EDTA in any third. In both combined protocols smear layer was greatest apically (p < 0.001). Images completely covered by smear layer could not be segmented, so open tubules were quantified in only 20-23 of 45 specimens per third, without significant differences between the combined protocols. Erosion was assessable in only 28 of 135 images and was reported descriptively. CONCLUSIONS: With syringe irrigation, neither chlorine-based irrigant removed the smear layer without a chelator. EDTA significantly reduced smear layer with 5.25% NaOCl, but no significant contribution was detected with 200 ppm HOCl in this sample. These findings do not support replacing NaOCl with HOCl and agree with existing evidence supporting NaOCl followed by EDTA as the reference protocol.
